source_refs.note: Book p. 111-114: solids of revolution, disk method about the x- and y-axes, cross-sectional method, Examples 62-65, Figures 3.13-3.16

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Aaj ka sabaq bohat dilchasp hai. Kumhaar (potter) ko chaak par mitti ka bartan banate dekha hai? Woh mitti ka ek tukda ghoomte hue chaak par rakh kar haath se us ki ek side ki shakal deta hai, aur ghoomne ki wajah se poora gol bartan ban jata hai. Bilkul yahi "solid of revolution" hai: ek flat (plane) region ko kisi line ke gird ghumao to ek teen-dimensional solid ban jata hai.
Is lesson mein hum seekhenge ke aise solid ka volume integral se kaise nikalte hain: pehle \(x\)-axis ke gird ghumane wala disk method, phir \(y\)-axis ke gird, aur aakhir mein cross-sectional method jo har tarah ke slices ke liye kaam karta hai. Phir kitab ki chaar misaalein hal karenge.
Kisi cheez ka volume physical sciences ke bohat se masail mein ahem kirdar ada karta hai. Is section mein hum solids of revolution ka volume nikalne ke tareeqe dekhenge.

Agar kisi plane (sat'h) mein ek region ko usi plane ki kisi line ke gird ghumaya (revolve kiya) jaye to jo solid banta hai use solid of revolution kehte hain, aur kehte hain ke yeh solid us region se generate hua hai. Jis line ke gird ghumate hain use axis of revolution kehte hain. Khaas taur par, agar Figure 3.13(a) wale region ko \(x\)-axis ke gird ghumayein to Figure 3.13(b) wala solid milta hai. Agar \(x\)-axis ke perpendicular ek plane is solid ko kaate to kata hua hissa (section) ek circle hota hai, aur is soorat mein volume disk method se nikalta hai jo neeche ke do boxed results mein bayan hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab yahan "theorem 3.10 and 3.11" ka hawala deti hai, lekin in numbers ke koi theorems kitab mein chhape hi nahi. Disk method neeche wale do boxed results mein diya gaya hai (ek \(x\)-axis ke gird, doosra \(y\)-axis ke gird).

blocks.alt: Left: a region R under a curve y = f(x) above the x-axis from x = a to x = b. Right: the solid obtained by rotating R about the x-axis, with circular ends at a and b and a dashed circular cross-section in between.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.13: (a) the region R, (b) the solid generated by rotating R about the x-axis (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Maan lein \(f\) interval \([a, b]\) par continuous aur non-negative (kabhi negative nahi) hai, aur \(R\) woh region hai jo \(y = f(x)\) ke graph, \(x\)-axis aur khari lines \(x = a\) aur \(x = b\) se ghira hai. \(R\) ko \(x\)-axis ke gird ghumane se bane solid ka volume \(V\) yeh hai:

blocks.text_alt: V equals the integral from a to b of pi times f of x squared, d x

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh formula kahan se aaya? Solid ko \(x\)-axis ke perpendicular bohat patli patli gol tikiyon (disks) mein kaat lein, jaise sikkon ka dher ya kheere ke gol slices. \(x\) par wali tikiya ka radius \(r = f(x)\) aur motai \(dx\) hai. Cylinder ka volume (base ka area) \(\times\) (unchai) hota hai, to is tikiya ka volume
\[\pi r^2 \times \text{motai} = \pi[f(x)]^2\,dx\]
\(a\) se \(b\) tak saari tikiyon ka jama yahi integral hai. Ghaur karein: radius ka square hota hai, region ke area ka nahi.

Isi tarah, maan lein \(g\) interval \([c, d]\) par continuous aur non-negative hai, aur \(R\) woh region hai jo \(x = g(y)\) ke graph, \(y\)-axis aur horizontal lines \(y = c\) aur \(y = d\) se ghira hai. \(R\) ko \(y\)-axis ke gird ghumane se bane solid ka volume yeh hai:

blocks.text_alt: V equals the integral from c to d of pi times g of y squared, d y

blocks.alt: Left: a region between the y-axis and the curve x = g(y) from y = c to y = d. Right: the vase-shaped solid obtained by rotating it about the y-axis, with circular ends at c and d and a circular cross-section in between.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.14: the region bounded by x = g(y), y = c, y = d and the y-axis, and the solid generated about the y-axis (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yaad rakhne ka aasaan asool: integration ka variable hamesha axis of revolution ke saath saath chalta hai.
\(x\)-axis ke gird: radius \(= y = f(x)\), integrate \(dx\) ke saath, limits \(x\) ki values.
\(y\)-axis ke gird: radius \(= x = g(y)\), integrate \(dy\) ke saath, limits \(y\) ki values. Is liye pehle \(y = f(x)\) ko \(x = g(y)\) mein badalna parta hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar \(y = \sqrt{x}\) ko \(x = 0\) se \(x = 4\) tak \(x\)-axis ke gird ghumayein to volume kya hoga? Radius \(\sqrt{x}\), us ka square \(x\), to \(V = \pi\int_0^4 x\,dx = \pi \cdot \frac{16}{2} = 8\pi\). (Yeh hamari taraf se misaal hai.) Dekha, square karne se square root khatam ho gaya aur integral bohat aasaan ho gaya.
Volume of Solid of Revolution by Cross-sectional Method

Maan lein \(S\) ek solid hai jo planes \(P_a\) aur \(P_b\) ke darmiyan hai. Agar plane \(P_x\) mein \(S\) ke cross-section ka area \(A(x)\) ho, aur \(A\) continuous function ho, to \(S\) ka volume yeh hai:

blocks.text_alt: V equals the integral from a to b of A of x d x

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh aam (general) asool hai; disk method is ki ek khaas soorat hai jahan har slice circle hota hai, \(A(x) = \pi[f(x)]^2\). Jab slices kisi aur shakal ke hon (square, triangle, semicircle) to yeh tareeqa use karein. Socho double roti: har slice ki shakal kuch bhi ho, us ka area \(\times\) motai jor do to poori roti ka volume.
Plan: (1) base ka sketch, (2) ek slice ka size \(x\) mein likhna, (3) \(A(x)\) banana, (4) solid ke dono siron ke beech integrate karna.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Disk method se sphere (gend) ka mashhoor formula khud nikaal kar dekhte hain. Radius \(r\) wala aadha circle \(y = \sqrt{r^2 - x^2}\), \(x = -r\) se \(x = r\) tak, \(x\)-axis ke gird ghumayein to poora sphere ban jata hai.
\[V = \pi\int_{-r}^{r} (r^2 - x^2)\,dx\]
\[= \pi\left[r^2 x - \dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-r}^{r}\]
\[= \pi\left(\dfrac{2r^3}{3} + \dfrac{2r^3}{3}\right) = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3\]
Yahi woh formula hai jo aap school se ratte aa rahe hain; ab aap jante hain ke yeh aaya kahan se.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Example 62 ko samajhne ke liye pehle tasveer zehan mein banaiye. Zameen par radius 2 ka ek gol plate rakha hai (yeh base hai). Ab is plate par \(x\)-axis ke perpendicular bohat saare patle equilateral triangles khare kar dein, har triangle ka base plate ki ek chord par ho. Beech mein chord sab se lambi (4) hai, is liye wahan triangle sab se bara hai; kinaron ki taraf chords chhoti hoti jati hain aur triangles bhi. In sab triangles ko jor dein to ek tent jaisa solid banta hai. Figure 3.15 mein (a) yahi solid, (b) us ka base aur (c) ek triangle dikhaya gaya hai.

blocks.title: Example 62
blocks.problem: A solid has a circular base of radius 2. Parallel cross-sections perpendicular to the base are equilateral triangles. Find the volume of the solid.
steps:
Diya gaya: ek solid jis ka base radius 2 wala circle hai; base ke perpendicular (amoodi) har cross-section ek equilateral triangle (teenon sides barabar) hai.
Maloom karna: volume \(V\).
Tareeqa: cross-sectional method, \(V = \int_a^b A(x)\,dx\). Pehle centre se \(x\) faasle par wale triangle ka area \(A(x)\) nikalenge, phir \(-2\) se \(2\) tak integrate karenge.

Step 1: Base ko coordinates mein likhein
Base ko origin par centre wala circle lete hain:
\[x^2 + y^2 = 4\]
\(x\) faasle par cross-section chord \(AB\) par khara hai (Figure 3.15 (b)). \(B\) circle par hai, is liye
\[y = \sqrt{4 - x^2}\]
\[|AB| = 2y\]
Kyun: chord \((x, -y)\) se \((x, y)\) tak jati hai, to us ki lambai \(y - (-y) = 2y\) hai. Yahi triangle ka base hai.

Step 2: Triangle ki unchai
Triangle \(ABC\) equilateral hai aur us ki har side \(2y\) hai. Unchai \(CD\):
\[CD = \sqrt{(2y)^2 - y^2} = \sqrt{3}\,y\]
Kyun: \(D\) chord \(AB\) ka beech ka point hai, to triangle \(ADC\) right-angled hai jis ka hypotenuse \(2y\) aur base \(y\) hai. Pythagoras se \(\sqrt{4y^2 - y^2} = \sqrt{3y^2} = \sqrt{3}\,y\) (Figure 3.15 (c)). Yaad rakhein: side \(s\) wale equilateral triangle ki unchai hamesha \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}s\) hoti hai.

Step 3: Cross-section ka area
\[A(x) = \dfrac{1}{2}(\text{Base})(\text{Height})\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 2y \cdot \sqrt{3}\,y = \sqrt{3}\,y^2\]
\[= \sqrt{3}\,(4 - x^2)\]
Kyun: circle se \(y^2 = 4 - x^2\). Ab area sirf \(x\) par depend karta hai, aur integration \(dx\) ke saath ho sakti hai.
Dhyan dein: \(y\) ko \(x\) mein badalna zaroori hai; \(y\) rehne diya to integral \(dx\) ke saath nahi chalega.

Step 4: Poore base par integrate karein
\[V = \int_{-2}^{2} A(x)\,dx\]
\[= \int_{-2}^{2} \sqrt{3}\,(4 - x^2)\,dx\]
\[= \sqrt{3}\left[4x - \dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-2}^{2}\]
Kyun: solid diameter ke ek sire \(x = -2\) se doosre sire \(x = 2\) tak phaila hua hai. Socho double roti (bread) ke slices: har slice ek patla triangle hai jis ki motai \(dx\) hai, aur saare slices jor kar poori roti banti hai.

Step 5: Limits lagayein
\[= \sqrt{3}\left[\left(8 - \dfrac{8}{3}\right) - \left(-8 + \dfrac{8}{3}\right)\right]\]
\[= \sqrt{3}\left[8 - \dfrac{8}{3} + 8 - \dfrac{8}{3}\right]\]
\[= \sqrt{3} \cdot \dfrac{32}{3} = \dfrac{32\sqrt{3}}{3}\]
Kyun: \(x = -2\) par \(4(-2) - \frac{(-2)^3}{3} = -8 + \frac{8}{3}\); us ko minus karne se dono terms ke sign badal gaye.

Tasdeeq:
\(4 - x^2\) even function hai (\(x\) aur \(-x\) par ek hi value), is liye \(V = 2\sqrt{3}\int_0^2 (4 - x^2)\,dx = 2\sqrt{3}\left(8 - \frac{8}{3}\right) = \frac{32\sqrt{3}}{3} \approx 18.48\). Wohi jawab.

blocks.alt: Three panels. (a) An oblique sketch of the solid: a circular base of radius 2 with equilateral triangles standing on chords perpendicular to the x-axis. (b) The base circle x squared plus y squared equals 4 with a vertical chord AB at distance x from the origin, half-length y. (c) The equilateral triangle ABC with base 2y, height root 3 times y, foot D and 60 degree angles.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.15: (a) the solid, (b) its base, (c) a cross-section (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Example 63
blocks.problem: Find the volume of the solid obtained by rotating the region bounded by \(y = x^3\), \(y = 64\), and \(x = 0\) around the \(y\)-axis.
steps:
Diya gaya: region jo \(y = x^3\), \(y = 64\) aur \(x = 0\) (yani \(y\)-axis) se ghira hai.
Maloom karna: is region ko \(y\)-axis ke gird ghumane se bane solid ka volume.
Tareeqa: \(y\)-axis ke gird disk method, \(V = \int_c^d \pi[g(y)]^2\,dy\). Yahan disks leti hui (horizontal) hain, is liye curve ko \(x = g(y)\) ki shakal mein likhna hoga.

Step 1: Curve ko \(x = g(y)\) mein likhein
\[y = x^3 \Rightarrow x = y^{1/3}\]
Region aur solid, ek typical disk ke saath, Figure 3.16 mein dikhaye gaye hain.
Kyun: height \(y\) par wali disk ka radius woh faasla hai jo \(y\)-axis se curve tak hai, aur yeh faasla \(x\) hai. Is liye radius ko \(y\) mein likhna zaroori hai.

Step 2: Limits
Region \(y = 0\) se \(y = 64\) tak hai, yani \(c = 0\), \(d = 64\).
Kyun: \(x = 0\) par \(y = 0^3 = 0\), aur upar ki hadd line \(y = 64\) hai jo curve ko \((4, 64)\) par milti hai (\(4^3 = 64\)).
Dhyan dein: limits \(y\) ki hain (0 se 64), \(x\) ki nahi (0 se 4), kyunke integration \(dy\) ke saath hai.

Step 3: Integral banayein aur integrate karein
\[V = \int_0^{64} \pi\left(y^{1/3}\right)^2 dy\]
\[= \pi\int_0^{64} y^{2/3}\,dy\]
\[= \pi\left[\dfrac{3}{5}y^{5/3}\right]_0^{64}\]
Kyun: power ki power: \(\left(y^{1/3}\right)^2 = y^{2/3}\). Phir power rule: power mein 1 jama karo (\(\frac{2}{3} + 1 = \frac{5}{3}\)) aur nayi power se divide karo, yani \(\frac{3}{5}\) se multiply.

Step 4: Limits lagayein
\[= \dfrac{3\pi}{5}\left[(64)^{5/3} - 0\right]\]
\[= \dfrac{3\pi}{5}\left[(4^3)^{5/3}\right] = \dfrac{3\pi}{5}(4^5)\]
\[= \dfrac{3\pi}{5}(1024) = \dfrac{3072\pi}{5}\]
Kyun: \(64 = 4^3\), is liye \(64^{5/3}\) mein pehle cube root (4) aur phir power 5: \(4^5 = 1024\).

Tasdeeq:
Hamari taraf se ek aur tareeqa (shell method, kitab mein nahi): \(V = 2\pi\int_0^4 x(64 - x^3)\,dx = 2\pi\left(512 - \frac{1024}{5}\right) = \frac{3072\pi}{5} \approx 1930.2\). Bilkul wohi jawab.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Example 63 ke hal mein kitab "Figure 16" likhti hai; figure ka asal caption Figure 3.16 hai.

blocks.alt: Left: the region between the y-axis and the curve y = x cubed, from y = 0 to y = 64, with a horizontal strip marked as a typical disk; the point (4, 64) is marked. Right: the bowl-shaped solid formed by rotating this region about the y-axis, with the disk shown as a circle.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.16: the region bounded by y = x³, y = 64 and x = 0, and the solid with a typical disk (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar Example 63 wala region \(y\)-axis ke bajaye \(x\)-axis ke gird ghumaya jaye to kya badlega? Ab disks khari hongi, integration \(dx\) ke saath hogi aur limits \(x = 0\) se \(x = 4\) hongi. Lekin dhyan dein: yeh region curve ke upar aur line \(y = 64\) ke neeche hai, is liye har slice ek chhalla (washer, beech mein surakh wali tikiya) banega, poori disk nahi. Aise sawal aap aage ki classes mein karenge; abhi sirf itna samajh lein ke axis badalne se poora setup badal jata hai, is liye pehle hamesha sketch dekhiye.

blocks.title: Example 64
blocks.problem: A cone is formed by rotating the straight line \(y = 2x\) around the \(x\)-axis from \(x = 0\) to \(x = 5\) cm. Find the volume of the cone.
steps:
Diya gaya: seedhi line \(y = 2x\), jo \(x = 0\) se \(x = 5\) cm tak \(x\)-axis ke gird ghumai jati hai.
Maloom karna: is se bane cone (makhrooti shakal, jaise ice cream ki cone) ka volume.
Tareeqa: \(x\)-axis ke gird disk method, \(V = \int_a^b \pi[f(x)]^2\,dx\), jahan \(f(x) = 2x\), \(a = 0\), \(b = 5\).

Step 1: Integral banayein
\[V = \pi\int_0^5 (2x)^2\,dx\]
\[= \pi\int_0^5 4x^2\,dx = 4\pi\int_0^5 x^2\,dx\]
Kyun: \(x\) par wali disk ka radius line ki unchai \(2x\) hai, is liye us ka area \(\pi(2x)^2 = 4\pi x^2\). Constant \(4\pi\) ko integral se bahar nikal liya.
Dhyan dein: \((2x)^2 = 4x^2\) hai, \(2x^2\) nahi.

Step 2: Integrate karein aur limits lagayein
\[= 4\pi\left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^5\]
\[= 4\pi\left(\dfrac{5^3}{3} - 0\right) = 4\pi\left(\dfrac{125}{3}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{500\pi}{3} \approx 523.6\]
Kyun: power rule se \(\int x^2 dx = \frac{x^3}{3}\); \(\pi \approx 3.1416\) rakhne se \(\frac{500 \times 3.1416}{3} \approx 523.6\).

Tasdeeq:
Yeh solid ek cone hai jis ki unchai 5 cm aur base ka radius \(2(5) = 10\) cm hai. School wala formula: \(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi(100)(5) = \frac{500\pi}{3}\). Bilkul wohi jawab; is se pata chalta hai ke disk method sahi kaam kar raha hai.

blocks.title: Example 65
blocks.problem: A mug is designed by rotating the line \(y = 3x + 1\) around the \(x\)-axis from \(x = 0\) to \(x = 4\) cm. Find the volume of the mug.
steps:
Diya gaya: line \(y = 3x + 1\), jo \(x = 0\) se \(x = 4\) cm tak \(x\)-axis ke gird ghumai jati hai.
Maloom karna: is se bane mug ka volume.
Tareeqa: disk method, \(V = \int_a^b \pi[f(x)]^2\,dx\), jahan \(f(x) = 3x + 1\), \(a = 0\), \(b = 4\).

Step 1: Integral banayein aur square kholein
\[V = \pi\int_0^4 (3x + 1)^2\,dx\]
\[= \pi\int_0^4 (9x^2 + 6x + 1)\,dx\]
Kyun: \((a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2\) se \((3x + 1)^2 = 9x^2 + 6x + 1\). Square khol dene se har term par alag power rule lag jata hai.
Dhyan dein: beech wala term \(2 \times 3x \times 1 = 6x\) bhoolna nahi.

Step 2: Integrate karein
\[= \pi\left[\dfrac{9x^3}{3} + \dfrac{6x^2}{2} + x\right]_0^4\]
\[= \pi\left[3x^3 + 3x^2 + x\right]_0^4\]
Kyun: har term par power rule; \(\frac{9}{3} = 3\) aur \(\frac{6}{2} = 3\) se expression saaf ho gaya.

Step 3: Limits lagayein
\[= \pi\left[\left(3(4)^3 + 3(4)^2 + 4\right) - 0\right]\]
\[= \pi[192 + 48 + 4] = 244\pi\]
Kyun: \(3 \times 64 = 192\), \(3 \times 16 = 48\); \(x = 0\) par sab terms zero.

Tasdeeq:
Yeh solid ek frustum hai (cone jis ki nok kaat di gayi ho, jaise balti ya glass). Radii \(r_1 = 1\) (\(x = 0\) par) aur \(r_2 = 13\) (\(x = 4\) par), unchai 4. Frustum formula: \(\frac{\pi h}{3}(r_1^2 + r_1 r_2 + r_2^2) = \frac{4\pi}{3}(1 + 13 + 169) = \frac{4\pi}{3}(183) = 244\pi\). Wohi jawab.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Example 64 mein agar line \(y = 2x\) ke bajaye \(y = 3\) (seedhi horizontal line) ho aur \(x = 0\) se \(x = 5\) tak ghumayein, to kaunsa solid banega? Cylinder, jis ka radius 3 aur lambai 5 hai. Formula se: \(V = \pi\int_0^5 9\,dx = 45\pi\), aur school ka formula \(\pi r^2 h = \pi(9)(5) = 45\pi\). Dono ek jaise.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(x\)-axis ke gird disk method: \(V = \int_a^b \pi[f(x)]^2\,dx\).
2. \(y\)-axis ke gird disk method: \(V = \int_c^d \pi[g(y)]^2\,dy\), curve ko \(x = g(y)\) mein likh kar.
3. Cross-sectional method: \(V = \int_a^b A(x)\,dx\), jahan \(A(x)\) slice ka area hai.
4. Integration ka variable hamesha axis of revolution ke saath (ya slices ke perpendicular) chalta hai.
5. Aasaan solids ko school ke formulas se check karein: cone \(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\), frustum \(\frac{\pi h}{3}(r_1^2 + r_1 r_2 + r_2^2)\).
6. Volume cubic units mein hota hai; agar length cm mein di ho to jawab cm\(^3\) mein likhein, jaise Examples 64 aur 65 mein.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Radius ka square bhool jana: \(\int \pi f(x)\,dx\) ghalat hai; \(\int \pi[f(x)]^2\,dx\) sahi hai.
2. Square ghalat kholna: \((2x)^2 = 4x^2\), aur \((3x + 1)^2 = 9x^2 + 6x + 1\) hai, \(9x^2 + 1\) nahi.
3. \(y\)-axis ke gird ghuma kar bhi \(dx\) aur \(x\) wali limits laga dena.
4. Cross-sectional method mein \(A(x)\) ke andar \(y\) chhor dena; base ki equation se usay \(x\) mein badlein.
